original.target_description: Experiment 1 DFT–trustworthiness relationship: requested coefficient does not uniquely identify the regression simple slope versus the separate participant-level linear/quadratic follow-up tests.

notes: Identity independently verified from article header: What Is Typical Is Good: The Influence of Face Typicality on Perceived Trustworthiness; Carmel Sofer, Ron Dotsch, Daniel H. J. Wigboldus, Alexander Todorov; DOI 10.1177/0956797614554955. Primary published research article, Psychological Science 2015, 26(1), 39–47, copyright 2014; canonical text includes methods, results and references. No target PDF was supplied. Only assigned unfinished fields are populated; other fields and replication are placeholders. The printed β = 2.27 is explicitly the attractiveness DFT effect, and β = −1.54 is the DFT × judgment-type interaction; neither is a printed trustworthiness simple slope. Separate trustworthiness follow-ups report linear F = 8.08, p < .01, ηp2 = .26 and quadratic F = 7.30, p < .05, ηp2 = .24. The description does not identify which trustworthiness test is intended. No simple slope computed, and no p transferred between tests. N candidates for parent field-scope review only: 24 participants assigned to trustworthiness for the participant-level tests; 11 face stimuli for face-level mean judgments. Neither establishes the requested critical coefficient model N. No arithmetic or df-based derivation used.
